hints.title: Single Element Substitution Parity
hints.text: Comparing query(0, 1, 2, 3) with query(0, 1, 2, i) reveals whether element i equals element 3.

hints.title: Base Element Classification
hints.text: Use 4-element queries to classify every index i from 4 onwards as either matching element 3 or differing from it.

hints.title: Resolving Prefix Elements
hints.text: Query substituting index 3 with elements 0, 1, 2 to classify the first three indices.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of array in reader
complexity.notes: Requires exactly N queries to classify every element relative to element 3.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Querying all combinations of 4 elements causes combinatorial query explosion.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Fixing 3 anchor indices allows linear classification with N queries.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Relative equality classification by swapping one element in the 4-tuple query.
